manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the blue pen on the box and insert it into the pen holder on the right.

Task description: The target is the blue pen on the white box surface. Insert it into the white pen holder to the right, in front of the upright panel.

Success criteria: One end of the blue pen passes through the right-side pen holder opening, and the barrel extends into and remains in the holder. Merely touching the rim does not count as completion.

## Execution tips

- Consider grasping a straight section of the pen shaft with clearance on both sides, away from the clip and cap seam. Leave enough length exposed at the end that will be inserted, so the gripper does not hit the holder rim first.
- Close across the pen shaft and open slightly wider locally. Before closing, confirm the fingers are on opposite sides and pads can contact the shaft, avoiding mere image overlap or pressing it against the box surface.
- When adjusting the pen pose, rotate it slightly where there is clearance at both ends, reducing the risk of the tip brushing neighboring pens, the box surface, or the upright panel beside the holder.
- Objects already occupy the holder opening. Aim the pen's free end into a visible gap and feed it slowly along its long axis. If blocked by the rim or another object, retreat slightly and adjust rather than forcing it, which could cause slipping or tip the holder.
- Before releasing, confirm that the pen has entered the holder and is supported. Leave room for the fingertips to withdraw so the pen does not fall outside the holder or get pulled out by the gripper.

I have read the manual and identified the blue pen and white holder on the right. Only the right arm is available. I am orienting the gripper at height and approaching the pen, reducing steps near the box surface and confirming the grasp before transfer.

The gripper is above the blue pen, which remains separated from nearby objects. I will continue correcting finger alignment with the barrel and lower gradually, avoiding pressing the pen against the box surface.

The straight section of the blue pen is between the fingers, and a closure command has been sent. Next I will wait for the gripper to stabilize, then lift a short distance to check whether the pen leaves the box with it.

After a short lift, the blue pen moved with the gripper and the grasp remained stable, confirming it has been picked up. I am transporting it toward the pen holder and gradually turning it to an insertion-friendly pose.

An orientation adjustment triggered a recoverable controller singularity rejection after partial arm motion. The blue pen remains grasped. I will replan from the returned measured pose, retreat to a more reachable orientation within this episode, then adjust the insertion path.

An executable pose has been restored, and the blue pen remains stable. Existing objects and a vertical panel flank the pen-holder opening. Next I will align with the visible gap using moves no greater than 1 cm and check the pen end relative to the rim.

The blue pen remains securely grasped, and its tip is approaching the open space to the left of the pen holder. I am checking clearance between the gripper, partition, and rim using both views and continuing small position corrections.

Lateral motion reached the tool's workspace boundary; the out-of-bounds command was rejected without execution. I will adjust orientation and front/back position within bounds, using the pen's protruding length to continue aligning with the holder opening.
With a small rotation, the pen tip has moved from the left side of the opening to above it. Next I will lower slowly and release only after the tip is visibly inside the holder and supported.

The pen tip has lowered into the holder opening, and no noticeable movement of the holder or nearby objects is visible yet. The gripper still holds the pen; I will use smaller steps to confirm insertion depth.

From the head-camera view, the lower end of the blue pen has entered the opening and is obscured by the front wall of the holder, which remains stable. I will loosen the gripper slightly and check whether the pen stays inside before withdrawing it.
After release, the blue pen fell and remained inside the pen holder; it was not pulled out while withdrawing. I will move back a little farther to obtain an unobstructed view, then end this episode.
